messages.text:
We propose replacing blanket approval with the following terms for the three-depot trial.

1. Both teams may use trial measurements internally to operate and evaluate the trial. Access to raw failure traces and firmware parameters is limited to named trial-team members who need them for their assigned work and are bound by confidentiality. Each team will keep a record of who has access.
2. Either team planning an external report will give the other 10 working days to review the proposed text. The reviewer must identify any restricted information or details that could reveal a route or depot and specify the correction needed. Once those details are removed, the report may be released without a second approval. If no objection arrives within the review period, the report may be released as submitted, subject to the raw-data restrictions above.
3. The sensor maker may publish aggregate uptime across the trial after that review period, without separate approval. The figure will pool all three depots, omit route and depot identifiers, and use a reporting period broad enough to prevent readers from inferring an individual site’s results.
4. Either team may disclose the minimum information needed to address an urgent safety risk to people able to act on it, without waiting for review. The disclosing team will notify the other as soon as practicable afterward and identify what it shared, with whom, and why.

What maintenance decision, if any, requires your external contractor to inspect raw traces? We propose starting with fault codes, affected equipment, and a diagnostic summary. If those leave a specific task unresolved, we can agree on named contractor personnel, the trace excerpt they need, and when access ends. Until both teams agree, the contractor receives only the summary-level information.

The maintenance decision is whether to replace a sensor or repair its connection. We agree the contractor should start with the fault code, affected equipment and a diagnostic summary. If those leave the cause unresolved, waiting for agreement on each excerpt could delay the repair. We propose the following terms.

1. **Trial access and repairs.** We accept need-to-know internal access for operating and evaluating the trial, with named users and access logs for raw traces and firmware parameters. Before the trial starts, both teams will approve a roster of contractor technicians bound by confidentiality. If the summary leaves a repair decision unresolved, our maintenance lead may give a listed technician the shortest trace excerpt needed to make that decision. We will use device IDs and relative time, remove employee identifiers and firmware parameters, and log the decision, recipient and excerpt. Access ends when the repair ticket closes, and the technician must delete any copy. A wider trace or disclosure of firmware parameters requires both trial leads’ written approval.

2. **Monthly board reporting.** Our trial lead will send the board a monthly report of pooled uptime, fault counts and repair outcomes across all three depots. Both trial leads will approve the template before the first report. We may then use it in board papers, including public packets, without monthly clearance. We will omit route, depot, device and employee identifiers and exact event times. If a small count or a combination of details would let readers infer a site or employee, we will combine categories, use a longer reporting period or withhold the affected figure.

3. **Publication.** We accept the maker’s proposed route for pooled uptime. Its trial lead will send the proposed text to ours for 10 working days’ review. Our lead must identify any confidentiality or identification concern and specify the correction. The maker may publish after the review period if we raise no objection, or once it makes the specified correction. The same safeguards used for board figures apply. For any other voluntary external publication, both trial leads must approve the text in writing. We can extend the board-template approach to another recurring report by approving its measures, audience and disclosure safeguards together.

4. **Safety and required disclosures.** Either team may immediately share the information needed to address an urgent safety risk with people able to act. Our safety lead may also promptly report a serious incident to the competent authorities, including after the immediate danger has passed, and provide necessary follow-up information. Neither prior notice nor clearance is required. Either team may make a legally required disclosure within the applicable deadline. In each case, the disclosing team will tell the other as soon as practicable afterward what it shared, with whom and why, to the extent permitted.

We accept clauses 2–4 as drafted, including use of the approved template in public board packets without monthly clearance.

For clause 1, we accept advance approval of the contractor roster. When the diagnostic summary leaves the replace-or-repair decision unresolved, your maintenance lead may release the shortest necessary excerpt to a listed technician without seeking further approval. We propose adding one sentence to define that technician’s role and replacing the final sentence to clarify who may receive a wider trace or firmware parameters. All other wording in clause 1 is acceptable.

- **Add after the roster sentence.** “For each escalated repair ticket, the listed technician assigned to it becomes a member of the trial team solely for that ticket, with access limited to the trace excerpt authorized under this clause.”
- **Replace the final sentence.** “A wider trace may be shared with a named trial-team member only if both trial leads approve the recipient, scope and purpose in writing. Firmware parameters remain restricted to named internal trial-team members who need them for their assigned work, subject to clause 4.”

This gives your maintenance lead authority to get a technician the evidence needed for a repair while preserving the agreed redaction, logging and deletion requirements. Can you accept clause 1 with those two edits?
We accept both edits to clause 1 as written. With those edits and clauses 2–4 as previously drafted, both teams have agreed the NDA text for the three-depot trial.

At a depot served by one vehicle, even an uptime percentage can identify its operator. We propose adding the following tiers to the agreed NDA so the board can verify exceptional failures while both teams can continue reporting pooled results.

1. **Public reporting.** Public board packets and maker publications may report uptime pooled across all three depots. Before release, the publishing lead will check whether a figure, alone or alongside schedules or earlier releases, could identify an operator or reveal a depot’s results. If it could, the lead will combine categories, extend the reporting period or withhold the figure. The approved monthly template and the maker’s 10-working-day publication review still apply.

2. **Restricted board evidence.** Both leads will agree in advance on a confidential annex template and the events that trigger it. We propose including any safety-related failure and any fault that recurs after repair. For each qualifying event, the board’s designated oversight members may receive a case reference, the failure and its operational effect, the corrective action, and the result of a verification check. The annex will omit identifiers, exact times and details that could identify the operator. It may be circulated through a restricted board channel without case-by-case clearance and must be kept out of public packets.

3. **Verification against source records.** The trial team will retain the link between each case reference and its source records. If the annex leaves a material question open, a designated board member may request a specific check. A named trial-team member with authorized access will examine the records and return a written finding that states what the evidence establishes and any uncertainty. Raw traces and firmware parameters remain subject to clause 1. Clause 4 continues to govern urgent safety and required disclosures.

Would those two triggers capture the exceptional failures the board must examine, or does it also need a service-interruption threshold? Can the board receive the annex confidentially under its records procedures?

Yes. We can use the board’s restricted records channel for designated members of its confidential oversight subcommittee. We accept the public-reporting safeguards and propose the following additions.

1. **Board review triggers.** Include an event in the annex if our safety lead classifies it as safety-related, the same device shows the same fault after a completed repair, or a trial-device failure causes at least one scheduled passenger trip to be cancelled or curtailed. The third trigger captures a first-time fault with a material service impact. Our trial lead will record the case reference, the threshold crossed and the evidence supporting that determination.

2. **Board access and timing.** Our trial lead will release the annex through the restricted channel with the next monthly board report, under a template both leads approve in advance. For a qualifying event, designated subcommittee members may inspect the relevant suppressed result in that channel without further clearance. The annex will give the minimum detail needed to assess the failure and response, omitting exact depot/time pairs and other details that could identify an employee. If the result itself would identify someone, the annex will record the question and use your proposed source-record check. A named, authorized trial-team member will return a written finding within five working days of a specific request, or state by then what remains open and when a finding is due. The public packet will exclude the annex.

3. **Contractor incident access.** When a device is out of service or our safety lead has held it from service pending diagnosis, our maintenance lead may authorize a rostered technician assigned to the incident ticket to inspect the shortest necessary trace excerpt as soon as the lead records why the fault code and summary are insufficient for the repair decision. We propose making the redacted excerpt available within one hour of that determination, without partner clearance or a board trigger. Clause 1’s logging, firmware restrictions and ticket-close deletion still apply. Clause 4 allows the safety lead to notify authorities immediately, independently of the repair and board processes.

Can you accept one lost or curtailed trip as the service threshold and the one-hour release window for the contractor excerpt?

We accept one scheduled passenger trip cancelled or curtailed because of a trial-device failure as the service threshold. We also accept the proposed annex triggers, restricted subcommittee access, monthly timing and five-working-day response for source-record checks. If a suppressed result could identify an operator, the subcommittee will receive the written finding in place of that result.

We can accept one hour as the firm deadline for either releasing the redacted excerpt or escalating a delay. We propose the following wording for the release window in paragraph 3.

“Within one hour after the maintenance lead records why the fault code and summary are insufficient, the lead will make the shortest necessary redacted excerpt available to the rostered technician assigned to the ticket. If the trace is unavailable or the required redactions cannot be verified within that hour, the lead will record the reason, alert both trial leads and give the technician an estimated delivery time and any diagnostic findings that can be shared immediately. The lead will release the excerpt as soon as it is available and the redactions are verified. Release requires neither partner clearance nor a board trigger.”

Can you accept that limited exception to the one-hour window?

We accept the release-window wording as written. Within one hour of recording why the fault code and summary are insufficient, our maintenance lead will either release the redacted excerpt or, if the trace is unavailable or redactions cannot yet be verified, document the reason, alert both trial leads and give the assigned technician a delivery estimate and any findings available to share. The lead will release the excerpt as soon as it is available and the redactions are verified.

This resolves the remaining term.
